items.title: CVE-2026-20079: Cisco Cisco Firewall Management Center Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability

items.title: PoisonedRefresh: A Fileless Linux Rootkit That Injects PHP Web Shells Into F5 BIG-IP APM Server Memory
items.one_liner: A sophisticated fileless Linux rootkit injects PHP web shells directly into F5 BIG-IP server memory via CVE-2025-53521.
items.summary: SophosLabs and ESET have detailed a stealthy, fileless Linux rootkit dubbed PoisonedRefresh (tracked as Linux/Agnt-IC) targeting F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager environments. The campaign exploits CVE-2025-53521, an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in BIG-IP APM when access policies are configured on virtual servers. The malware utilizes a modified Linux binary to infect Apache, modify SELinux settings, and persist across device upgrade cycles. It intercepts execution via __libc_start_main and hooks the Apache Portable Runtime module loader to inject a PHP web shell directly into libphp memory without writing artifacts to disk. Additionally, it provisions a local UNIX domain socket to spawn interactive bash sessions without opening listening TCP ports.
key_facts: Vulnerable Exposure: 795 internet-exposed endpoints observed by Shadowserver
items.bottom_line: PoisonedRefresh is a fileless Linux rootkit that evades artifact detection by injecting PHP web shells directly into F5 BIG-IP APM memory via CVE-2025-53521.

items.title: Chaotic Eclipse Released ShieldCrash, A PoC For Microsoft Defender Zero-Day
items.one_liner: A new Microsoft Defender zero-day PoC named ShieldCrash achieves arbitrary file read as SYSTEM despite September 2026 patches.
items.summary: Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse has published a proof-of-concept (PoC) zero-day exploit named ShieldCrash, targeting Microsoft Defender. The researcher demonstrates that Microsoft's security updates failed to completely remediate the ShieldBreak vulnerability (CVE-2026-69414) in the Microsoft Malware Protection Engine, leaving a specific condition unpatched. The exploit allows unprivileged users to execute an arbitrary file read with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges across all supported Windows versions, including fully updated systems running September 2026 security patches. Microsoft recommends keeping antimalware definitions and the engine automatically updated, though the default protections do not block this specific unpatched bypass.

Privilege Level: SYSTEM arbitrary file read

items.title: Google warns of new Chrome zero-day bug exploited in attacks
items.one_liner: A critical actively exploited Chrome zero-day demands immediate browser updates across all supported desktop platforms.
items.summary: Google has issued security updates patching 230 vulnerabilities, which includes a high-severity zero-day flaw tracked as CVE-2026-87491 that is actively exploited in the wild. Reported by researcher Jihyeon Jeong, the out-of-bounds write weakness affects the Chrome V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine across Windows, Mac, and Linux. Remote attackers can leverage crafted HTML pages to trigger heap corruption, achieve arbitrary code execution inside the browser sandbox, or cause application crashes. This marks the seventh actively exploited Chrome zero-day vulnerability patched by Google since the beginning of the year. The updates are currently rolling out to the Stable Desktop channel.
key_facts: Vulnerability Type: Out-of-bounds write in V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine
items.bottom_line: Google has patched its seventh actively exploited Chrome zero-day of the year, a V8 engine out-of-bounds write vulnerability designated CVE-2026-87491.

items.title: Chinese AI firms are siphoning capabilities from American models, CISA warns
items.one_liner: CISA and intelligence agencies warn that Chinese AI companies are aggressively distilling capabilities from U.S. frontier models at industrial scale.
items.summary: A joint cybersecurity advisory from CISA, NSA, and FBI warns that Chinese AI firms are utilizing large-scale knowledge distillation campaigns to siphon capabilities from U.S. frontier models. Companies including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI have extracted billions of tokens through millions of requests targeting variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok. These campaigns use API proxy 'transfer stations' and account pools to bypass geographic restrictions and obscure their origins, enabling rapid capability gains in reasoning and coding.

items.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
items.one_liner: OpenAI claims an unreleased internal model solved the 90-year-old Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem with a formal Lean proof.
items.summary: OpenAI announced that an internal AI model more capable than GPT-6 Astra has resolved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of mathematics' Millennium Prize Problems. The AI established statements C and D by constructing an analytical proof and Lean formalization demonstrating that initially smooth fluid dynamics can develop a finite-time singularity. The breakdown manifests as an inward spiraling, elongating vortex where velocity becomes unbounded despite finite energy. The company has published both the detailed proof writeup and the formal Lean verification code.

items.bottom_line: AI formal reasoning systems have advanced to solving major unsolved Millennium Prize mathematics problems with machine-checked proofs.

items.title: **Subject:** CVE-2026-2035703: Tozed ZLT X300 5G CPE — Unauthenticated Remote Root Code Execution via TR-069 Command Injection (CVSS 9.8)
items.one_liner: A critical CVSS 9.8 TR-069 command injection in Tozed ZLT X300 5G routers allows unauthenticated root RCE via rogue LTE base stations.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Nadeem Danish has publicly disclosed an unauthenticated remote root command injection vulnerability in Tozed ZLT X300 and X300A 5G CPE routers running firmware version 6.01.3, tracked as CVE-2026-2035703 with a CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw exists in the TR-069/CWMP client daemon (netcwmpd), where the IPPingDiagnostics Host parameter is passed unsanitized into a sprintf function and subsequently executed with root privileges via system_by_root(). An attacker utilizing a rogue LTE base station built with software-defined radio hardware costing approximately $300 can impersonate a carrier's Auto Configuration Server to achieve full root remote code execution without authentication. The vulnerability impacts carriers across 15 countries, and the vendor has refused to engage or provide a verified patch.
key_facts: Affected Product: Tozed ZLT X300 / X300A 5G CPE Router Firmware 6.01.3
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-2035703 is a critical unauthenticated root command injection vulnerability in Tozed ZLT X300 5G CPE routers exploitable via rogue LTE base stations.

items.title: Multiple Chinese hacking groups seen using identical Chrome zero-day exploit
items.one_liner: Multiple Chinese hacking groups are exploiting a Chrome zero-day via a shared exploit kit during the patch gap.
items.summary: At least four Chinese state-linked cyber-espionage groups have been exploiting the same zero-day Google Chrome vulnerability since late August using a shared exploit kit called BlueMoon. The flaw was fixed in open-source Chromium in early August, but a four-week patch gap before stable browser updates allowed attackers to reverse-engineer the patch and weaponize it. The exploit kit chains two browser flaws with a Windows bug to achieve code execution before dropping malware via crude curl commands. In response, Google is shifting Chrome to a two-week release cycle to accelerate security updates.
key_facts: Release Cycle Change: Moving Chrome to a two-week cycle
items.bottom_line: Google is shortening Chrome's release cycle to two weeks to eliminate the patch-gap exploited by threat actors using identical zero-day kits.

items.title: CVE-2026-87874 - Community.general: community.general: memcached cache plugin deserializes untrusted pickle data from memcached, enabling cache-poisoning remote code execution on the ansible controller
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-87874 allows RCE on Ansible controllers via insecure pickle deserialization in the memcached cache plugin.
items.summary: A high-severity flaw tracked as CVE-2026-87874 affects the memcached cache plugin of the community.general Ansible collection. Although documented to store records in JSON format, the plugin performs no explicit serialization and relies on python-memcached, which pickles values on write and unpickles them on read. Because memcached is unauthenticated and cache keys are predictable, attackers who can reach a network-exposed memcached instance can supply crafted pickle payloads that execute remote code on the Ansible controller when the fact cache is next read.
key_facts: Affected Component: community.general Ansible collection memcached cache plugin
items.bottom_line: Secure your memcached instances and avoid using unauthenticated memcached cache plugins that implicitly deserialize untrusted pickle data.

items.title: CVE-2026-87995 - Open WebUI: Same-origin XSS to account takeover via terminal port-preview iframe hardcoding allow-same-origin
items.one_liner: An XSS flaw in Open WebUI's terminal preview lets attackers hijack user accounts via hardcoded iframe permissions.
items.summary: Open WebUI versions between 0.8.11 and 0.11.1 contained an XSS-to-account-takeover vulnerability in the terminal port-preview component. The PortPreview component rendered terminal output inside an iframe sandbox with both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin enabled. Because the terminal proxy served the content from the same origin as Open WebUI, an authenticated user on a shared terminal server could host a script on a previewed port that hijacked victims' accounts. The issue was resolved in version 0.11.1.
items.bottom_line: Update Open WebUI to version 0.11.1 immediately to patch an account takeover vulnerability caused by insecure iframe sandbox flags.

items.one_liner: h3 before 1.15.9 is vulnerable to path traversal via double-encoded dot sequences in static file serving.
items.summary: Versions of h3 prior to 1.15.9 contain a path traversal vulnerability in the serveStatic utility due to a double-decoding flaw. items.bottom_line: Update h3 to version 1.15.9 or later to fix path traversal vulnerabilities in static asset retrieval.

items.one_liner: Critical unauthenticated SQL injection CVE-2026-72898 in Metabase password resets allows full database compromise.
items.summary: A critical, unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-72898 (GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf) has been disclosed in the password reset functionality of self-hosted Metabase instances. Carrying a maximum CVSS v3.1 score of 10.0, the flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary SQL against the application database via the POST /api/session/reset_password endpoint. Metabase has released patches across branches 58 through 63, and organizations must update immediately.

items.one_liner: North Korean threat actors implanted a sophisticated backdoor directly into HAProxy source code to target South Korean enterprise networks.
items.summary: North Korean-linked hackers have deployed a stealthy Linux backdoor embedded directly into the source code of HAProxy version 2.8.12 targeting South Korean automotive and media sectors. Discovered by Rapid7 Labs, the implant—dubbed the 'ted backdoor'—uses HAProxy's native filter API, event scheduler, and internal memory pools to intercept HTTP traffic and execute remote commands without leaving traces in application logs. items.title: Update on Attacks by Threat Group APT-C-60 in 2026
items.one_liner: APT-C-60 targets Japanese networks using Proton Drive links, LNK files, and legitimate developer CDNs for SpyGlace malware delivery.
items.summary: JPCERT/CC reported ongoing cyber espionage campaigns by threat group APT-C-60 targeting Japanese organizations in 2026. When opened, the LNK files execute obfuscated JavaScript, download script files via jsDelivr, and abuse legitimate developer utilities such as git.exe to pull downstream loaders and SpyGlace malware from platforms like GitLab and Codeberg. items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese threat actors leveraged an active Chrome zero-day and Windows kernel escape exploiting a temporary patch gap.
items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. The chain leveraged a reflected XSS on a US university website to redirect victims to a Google Chrome type-confusion zero-day in the V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), combined with a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the V8 sandbox and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to break out of the browser sandbox. Although CVE-2026-85046 had been fixed upstream in the Chromium codebase on August 4, 2026, a patch gap existed because no stable release of Google Chrome had incorporated the fix at the time of the attacks. Volexity discovered the activity and identified distinct post-exploitation payloads deployed by each actor.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion zero-day
CVE-2026-85880: Windows kernel privilege escalation / sandbox escape
items.bottom_line: Upstream code fixes do not protect users until a stable browser build is released, exposing a critical patch gap exploited by APT groups.

items.summary: Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) warns that both criminal groups and nation-state actors are aggressively using artificial intelligence to automate and scale attacks, effectively granting lesser-resourced groups nation-state-level capabilities. items.title: Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
items.one_liner: AI tools can now easily exploit a long-known vulnerability in voting scanners to deanonymize voter choices by correlating public records.
items.summary: A security vulnerability in voting machine scanners allows for the reconstruction of ballot order, which can be used to deanonymize voter behavior. By combining public early-voting lists with cast-vote record (CVR) files, an attacker can correlate specific voters with their ballot selections. The researcher successfully demonstrated this using an AI coding agent to process the data, confirming the vulnerability remains exploitable four years after initial disclosure. This poses a significant risk to ballot secrecy in jurisdictions that utilize the affected scanning technology.
key_facts: Method: Correlation of early-voting lists and CVR files
items.bottom_line: Publicly available cast-vote records, when combined with voter lists, allow for the deanonymization of individual ballots, undermining the privacy of the voting process.

items.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
items.one_liner: ServiceNow's 'Test Credential' feature can be abused to extract cleartext secrets, providing a critical post-exploitation path for red teams.
items.summary: Researchers at SpecterOps have identified a method to retrieve cleartext discovery credentials from ServiceNow instances by abusing the 'CredentialTestAjax' script include. By triggering an AJAX request to the /xmlhttp.do endpoint, an attacker can force the server to return secrets that are otherwise protected from direct UI or API access. This technique allows for the extraction of various credential types, including SSH keys and client secrets, which are stored in the discovery_credentials table. The research highlights a significant post-exploitation vector for attackers who have already gained a foothold in a ServiceNow environment.
items.bottom_line: If you manage ServiceNow instances, you must assume that any user with sufficient privileges to trigger credential tests can potentially extract cleartext secrets from the platform.

items.title: Your secrets are leaking to AI coding agents (and how to stop it)
items.one_liner: Critical security warning for developers using AI agents that ingest local context.
items.summary: AI coding agents are creating a new class of security risks by inadvertently leaking developer secrets like API keys and database passwords into LLM provider logs. Because these agents ingest local files and environment variables to build context, sensitive data is often included in the prompts sent to external models. Security researchers have also identified Shai-Hulud supply chain attacks that specifically target these agent sessions to exfiltrate credentials from local directories. Once a secret is leaked into a provider's history, it becomes extremely difficult to remediate as it persists in third-party logs. Developers are urged to implement secret detection at the prompt level to prevent sensitive data from leaving their local environment.
items.bottom_line: AI coding agents turn your local environment variables into permanent, logged prompts that are now being targeted by specialized malware.

items.title: Fake GTA6 ‘Leaked Download’ Caught Spreading RATs, Infostealer and Wiper Ransomware
items.one_liner: Fake GTA6 ISOs are spreading multiple RATs, infostealers, and a Chaos ransomware wiper via malicious installers.
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Huntress has uncovered a malware campaign exploiting anticipation for Grand Theft Auto VI by distributing fake ISO installers containing multiple Remote Access Trojans, an infostealer, and a wiper masquerading as ransomware. The malicious installers reach over 100GB through junk data padding and deploy NJRAT, DCRAT, Mercurial Grabber, and a Chaos ransomware variant used purely as a wiper. The campaign employs Russian-language prompts and targets Russian-speaking gamers with destructive payloads. This highlights how threat actors weaponize high-profile entertainment releases to deliver commodity malware.

Target product: Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA6)

items.title: Sebi eases commodity position limits, caps penalties for breaches
items.one_liner: Sebi doubles agricultural commodity position limits and rationalizes penalties for market participants.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has issued a circular easing position limits for agricultural commodity derivatives and revising penalty frameworks for violations. Under the updated guidelines, client-level position limits based on annual deliverable supply have been doubled to 2% for broad commodities, 1% for narrow commodities, and 0.5% for sensitive commodities. Penalties for position-limit breaches are now structured according to duration and excess percentage, capped at ₹2 lakh for severe violations over 2% and capped at ₹10,000 for smaller breaches. Additionally, Sebi expanded the definition of 'broad commodities' to include agricultural items with an average deliverable supply over five years of at least one million tonnes or ₹5,000 crore in monetary terms.
items.bottom_line: Commodity market participants benefit from doubled position limits and structured penalties following Sebi's regulatory revisions.

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has proposed governance changes for market infrastructure institutions (MIIs) to widen the talent pool for governing boards and standardize key managerial positions. Citing difficulties in finding qualified public interest directors due to strict disqualification rules stemming from group subsidiaries, Sebi proposed expanding exemptions to include companies with diversified shareholding where no single shareholder holds 10% or more. items.title: PEEP Turns Chrome and Edge Into Post-Compromise Backdoors for Host Command Execution
items.one_liner: PEEP uses forged Chromium Secure Preferences and native messaging binaries to turn Chrome and Edge into full host-level backdoors.
items.summary: Researchers disclosed details on PEEP, a Chromium-based post-exploitation framework derived from the open-source RedExt toolkit. Masquerading as a browser extension named 'Smart Bookmarks', PEEP bypasses Chrome Web Store checks and user prompts by manipulating Chromium's Secure Preferences integrity values. items.title: USN-8734-1: PHP vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: Ubuntu patched critical PHP bugs including a pgsql SQL injection flaw and multiple denial-of-service vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Ubuntu released advisory USN-8734-1 covering multiple vulnerabilities in PHP. A notable flaw, CVE-2026-17543, improperly escapes backslashes in the pgsql extension when standard_conforming_strings is active, allowing attackers to execute SQL injection attacks. Other fixed bugs include a NULL pointer dereference in SOAP Apache map decoding (CVE-2026-7262), an integer overflow in metaphone() (CVE-2026-7568), and unbounded recursion via circular symlinks in phar archives (CVE-2026-7260). Updated Ubuntu packages remediate these vulnerabilities.

items.bottom_line: Update PHP packages immediately if using PostgreSQL database extensions to prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities via backslash escaping.

items.one_liner: DPRK actors are deploying deep HAProxy backdoors and trojanized Linux system binaries against South Korean targets.
items.summary: Rapid7 Labs identified a sophisticated Linux espionage framework attributed to DPRK-nexus threat actors targeting South Korean automotive and media companies. The framework operates alongside trojanized Linux system binaries (crond, sshd, polkitd, agetty, atd), an SSH keylogger, and a curl-based RAT to establish deep persistence and avoid detection.

items.one_liner: A walkthrough details SSH brute-forcing, NTLM hash cracking, PrintSpoofer privilege escalation, and DACL manipulation in an eJPT CTF.
items.summary: This walkthrough of Post-Exploitation CTF 2 from INE's eJPT path details a multi-step compromise of a Windows target. The process begins with brute-forcing weak credentials for user 'alice' via SSH, extracting stored password hashes from hashdump.txt, and using John the Ripper to crack the NT hash for user 'david'. After gaining a shell as david, the author enumerates privileges and identifies enabled SeImpersonatePrivilege, which allows them to leverage PrintSpoofer to escalate privileges to SYSTEM. items.bottom_line: Misconfigured Windows service privileges like SeImpersonatePrivilege combined with weak user credentials allow rapid escalation from low-level access to SYSTEM.

items.summary: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has signed a decree lifting a decade-long suspension that prohibited citizens with legal permits from carrying firearms in public. items.one_liner: Update Perl HTML::FormHandler to 0.410002 to patch an unescaped attribute XSS vulnerability.
items.summary: A vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-85630, has been identified in Perl's HTML::FormHandler package prior to version 0.410002. The flaw exists because the process_attrs method renders field attributes into HTML without proper escaping when values are built from dynamic data rather than literals. This allows attackers to inject malicious JavaScript or override attributes, resulting in Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Developers are advised to upgrade to version 0.410002 or later.
items.bottom_line: Perl applications using HTML::FormHandler before 0.410002 are vulnerable to XSS due to unescaped field attributes rendered via process_attrs.

items.title: CVE-2026-19872: HTML::FormHandler versions before 0.410000 for Perl allow cross-site scripting via a submitted value rendered unescaped in an error message
items.one_liner: Perl library HTML::FormHandler versions prior to 0.410000 are vulnerable to XSS via unescaped form validation error messages.
items.summary: HTML::FormHandler versions before 0.410000 for Perl contain a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-19872. The library's error message renderers and wrappers interpolate error strings straight into HTML without entity escaping. When validation fails on fields using regular expressions, check lists, or type constraints, submitted user input is unescaped and reflected back in the error message, enabling script execution in the victim's origin. Operators must upgrade to version 0.410000 or later.
key_facts: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
items.bottom_line: Perl developers using HTML::FormHandler must upgrade to version 0.410000 immediately to prevent reflected cross-site scripting via form error handling.

items.title: Supreme Court allows Himachal to withdraw COVID-era cases against sitting and former MLAs
items.one_liner: India's Supreme Court clears the withdrawal of pandemic-era protest cases against Himachal Pradesh legislators.
items.summary: The Supreme Court of India has permitted the Himachal Pradesh government to withdraw criminal prosecutions against sitting and former legislators for minor offences and protests, such as burning effigies and highway dharnas, committed during the COVID-19 pandemic. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant reviewed a State challenge against a Himachal Pradesh High Court order that had previously permitted the dismissal of only 15 out of 65 total cases. The apex court noted that the pandemic represented an exceptional period of distress, and the alleged offenses involved no permanent property damage or injuries. Consequently, the remaining prosecutions under various sections of the IPC, National Highways Act, and Disaster Management Act can be withdrawn.

items.title: TryHackMe Injectics CTF Writeup: From SQL Injection to RCE
items.one_liner: A CTF walkthrough demonstrates chaining SQL injection against flawed client-side validation to manipulate background application logic.
items.summary: This article walks through the reconnaissance and exploitation stages of the Injectics CTF room on TryHackMe, demonstrating how to move from SQL injection to remote code execution. The author begins with Nmap and directory enumeration using gobuster, discovering developer comments revealing a background monitoring service that restores the users table with default credentials if deleted. Further inspection reveals a client-side JavaScript filter intended to block SQL injection keywords on the login form, which can be bypassed. By chaining these components, participants can target authentication mechanisms to progress toward the flag objectives.
items.bottom_line: Web application security assessments must never rely solely on client-side input filters to prevent critical injection flaws.

items.summary: The Attack Shark X6 Linux configurator project has received a significant update, moving from a DPI-only interface to a full-featured desktop companion supporting button remapping, lighting controls, and emergency resets. Built using Go and Wails v3 for the backend and React with Vite for the frontend, the beta application handles multi-device inventories over kernel-backed hidraw interfaces. It provides live status monitoring for battery heartbeats and physical DPI switches across eight stages ranging from 50 to 26000 DPI. Configuration reports are sent via SET_REPORT hidraw writes with debounced synchronization and versioned per-device persistence that survives application restarts. Users are instructed to install the packaged udev policy to grant user-level access without executing the utility with root privileges.

items.title: When to Use Encode-Prefill-Decode Disaggregation to Accelerate Multimodal Model Serving
items.summary: Encode-prefill-decode (EPD) disaggregation is an inference optimization technique for multimodal models that separates the vision encoder stage from the prefill and decode stages. It is most effective for image-heavy prompts, short-to-medium outputs, and quantized mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. This post shows when and how to use EPD disaggregation with NVIDIA Dynamo to achieve up to 5x faster time to first token (TTFT) and 7x faster end-to-end response time. The post also addresses the scenarios where EPD disaggregation is not recommended. Dynamo is an open source inference framework for serving AI models in distributed environments.
